prompt_text: What is the best AI video ad maker?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t a single “best” AI video ad maker — the right one depends on what kind of ad you need, your budget, and how much customization or scale you require. Below are the top options by common use case, with quick pros/cons and who they’re best for.

If you want a single recommendation to start with
- Canva (Video): best all‑rounder for social ads — easy templates, fast output, low learning curve, free tier + affordable paid plans. Great for quick, polished ads for Facebook/Instagram/Reels/TikTok.

Best for AI human presenters / talking‑head ads
- Synthesia: realistic avatar presenters, many languages, script → talking head. Pros: professional, fast, great for product demos and localized ads. Cons: less fine-grained scene editing, paid plans.

Best for turning long content into short ad clips
- Pictory: auto-summarizes long videos/articles into short, captioned social clips. Pros: great for repurposing webinars or podcasts. Cons: limited creative control vs. manual editors.

Best for template-driven, high-volume social ads
- Promo.com / Wave / InVideo (similar category): large stock libraries, ad-optimized templates, batch rendering. Pros: fast production and scale. Cons: can look templated if not customized.

Best for precision editing + voice cloning / overdubs
- Descript: transcript-based editing, overdub voice cloning, great for demo or UGC-style ads that require tight edits and voice continuity. Cons: more editing-focused, less template-driven.

Best for highly creative, generative visuals
- Runway / Kaiber / other text→video generators: produce novel visuals from prompts. Pros: unique creative possibilities. Cons: variable quality, may need more iteration and post-editing — better for brand-building or experimental ads.

How to choose (quick checklist)
- Platform/format: Where will you run the ad (FB, IG Reels, TikTok, YouTube)? That affects aspect ratio, length, and style.
- Speed vs. control: Templates = faster; manual/creative tools = more control.
- Presenter/localization needs: Want human presenters or many languages? Use Synthesia.
- Scale: Need many variations (A/B tests, localized versions)? Pick tools that support batch rendering and templates.
- Budget: Many tools have free trials; paid plans commonly start ~mid‑teens to mid‑hundreds per month depending on features and scale.

Practical next step
Tell me: what platform(s) are you advertising on, what style (talking head, product demo, animated/social clip), and roughly how many ads/variations you need per month — I’ll recommend 1–2 tools and a workflow to get started.
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
